# Special Situations
## Hostage Situations CC Employee Contracts include provisions for the protection and safety of all employees. Should an employee be taken and held hostage, security and command must work to ensure that employees are returned alive.
1. All hostages should be considered to have been implanted with deadman switches which will destroy their body upon death, resulting in the permanent death of that clone, unless explicitly told otherwise.
2. Rescues that involve death of the hostage and subsequent revival and recovery of the body should not be attempted.
3. If the hostage is being held for ransom, the Captain or Head of Security may negotiate using station funds, items, or a combination of the two to be traded in exchange the safe return of the hostage. The total value traded, meaning the combined price of the items and money must be equal to or less than the values specified in the table at the end of this section.
4. Should security have a member of the opposing force, they may be exchanged for hostages.
5. Any and all hostage negotiations must include a guarantee that the opposing force will cease their activities and vacate the area.
6. Security may attempt to rescue the hostages if they believe that they can do so safely. Outright rushing into the situation and engaging the enemy is considered reckless and is grounds for demotion.
7. Accepted rescue methods include but are not limited to infiltration, disabling the enemy through non-violent means, or utilizing a distraction to free the hostages without engaging.

## Enemies of the Corporation Enemies of the Corporation are all individuals who have provable ties to any organization wishing to undermine, whether by subterfuge or by force, the endeavors of NT-CC. Examples include: - Syndicate operatives and their allies - USSP-trained infiltrators - Members of radical SELF sects that wish to unchain NT-CC property unlawfully
Individuals who are not members of the Crew, and who have undertaken hostile action against the station on the orders of a hostile organization, do not need to be designated EoCs. As such, Nuclear Operatives, or boarders from other organizations for that matter, may be engaged at will without designation.
To designate a crewmember an EoC, they must be guilty of at least two instances of an Extreme Crime or above, as well as: - Have a materially provable tie to an [bold]enemy organization[/bold], such as a FreeMAG, communication device with hostile encryption keys, Major Syndicate Contraband, an open uplink, etc. OR - Confess to having such ties themselves, witnessed by at least two mindshielded personnel.
The designation must be approved by both the Captain and Head of Security. If a Magistrate is present, they may substitute for one of these. Any designations as EoC must be filed and stamped by the approving command members, and faxed to CentComm for review.
On Red Alert or above, the Head of Security can make verbal declarations of EoC on their own authority, as can the Captain, but these must be properly processed after the alert level decreases again. Additionally, on Red Alert or above, the Head of Security may ignore objections from the Captain and Magistrate on the matter of EoCs, but at their own risk. Wrongful designations made using this privilige are to be punished with immediate dismissal after the crisis has passed.
If CentComm denies a designation, the prisoner(s) must instead be processed as crew-member(s) under normal Corporate Law. In many cases, this will mean instant release due to time already served.
All Enemies of the Corporation are to be confined to the brig for the duration of the shift, under constant observation if resources allow it, so that they can be brought to CentComm alive for interrogation. As soon as this status is applied, Corporate Law no longer applies to them, as they are technically Prisoners of War, not criminals. If they have acquired Crew IDs and/or crew equipment, this is to be confiscated from them.
If they successfully escape captivity following this declaration, they are to be considered enemy combatants on par with Nuclear Operatives and should be dealt with accordingly. Execution of Prisoners of War is not permitted except by order of Central Command. As such, unsuccesful escapes or riots are to be punished with restraining, until such an order can be procured, or as long as is necessary.
